item.text: I’ll take a quick look at the repo shape first so I can ask a concrete refactor question instead of guessing blindly.

This is a very small app, with backend tag routes and a frontend PopularTags component path. I’m reading those files now to identify a low-risk cleanup target and preserve the untracked file already in the worktree.

The main cleanup opportunity is the tag-fetch flow: the service currently catches and swallows errors, which forces the component into an ambiguous “empty tags” state. I’m checking the project config before editing so the refactor matches the installed React/tooling versions.

I’m going to make a scoped refactor rather than invent structure this repo doesn’t need: keep behavior the same, make tag data explicit on the backend, let the frontend service either return a valid array or throw, and simplify the component states around loading/error/empty.
The refactor is in place. I’m doing a quick syntax/readback pass now; there’s no package manifest in this workspace, so verification will be limited to what can run directly here.
